headline: Structure and language models are probed for evolutionary and conformational limits
label: Protein Models For Molecular Evolution
summary: Protein structure and language models are now being audited against non-globular folds, mechanistic interpretability and evolutionary analysis tools.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how far protein structure and sequence models reflect evolutionary and biophysical reality. AlphaFold predictions for experimentally validated non-globular proteins diverge from biologically relevant structural states, which marks where predictions depart from the structures they are meant to represent. AlphaInterp dissects AlphaFold 3 and reports that a few divergent MSA homologues suffice to recover structure, tracing this through pairformer latent geometry and confidence outputs to locate the role of evolutionary information inside the model. A review of transformer protein foundation models covers residue dependencies, pathogenicity and alignment-free evolutionary analysis, while MolEvolvR provides a web app linking domain-centric searches, phylogenies and domain architecture across superkingdoms. What is new is the shift from reporting model performance toward mechanistic and biological scrutiny of what these models encode, paired with practical tools for evolutionary characterization.
